text: Introduction Purpose of dos.x: calculates the Density of States (DOS) (separated into up and down components for DSDA) Structure of the input data: ============================ &DOS ... / IMPORTANT: since v.5 namelist name is &DOS and no longer &INPUTPP

title: prefix
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: prefix of input file produced by pw.x (wavefunctions are not needed) Default: 'pwscf'

title: outdir
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: directory containing the input data, i.e. the same as in pw.x Default: value of the ESPRESSO_TMPDIR environment variable if set; current directory ('./') otherwise

title: bz_sum
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: Keyword selecting the method for BZ summation. Available options are: 'smearing' integration using gaussian smearing. In fact currently any string not related to tetrahedra defaults to smearing; 'tetrahedra' Tetrahedron method, Bloechl's version: P.E. Bloechl, PRB 49, 16223 (1994) Requires uniform grid of k-points, to be automatically generated in pw.x. 'tetrahedra_lin' Original linear tetrahedron method. To be used only as a reference; the optimized tetrahedron method is more efficient. 'tetrahedra_opt' Optimized tetrahedron method: see M. Kawamura, PRB 89, 094515 (2014). Default: 'smearing' if degauss is given in input; options read from the xml data file otherwise. 'smearing' 'tetrahedra' 'tetrahedra_lin' 'tetrahedra_opt'

title: ngauss
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: Type of gaussian broadening: = 0 Simple Gaussian (default) = 1 Methfessel-Paxton of order 1 = -1 "cold smearing" (Marzari-Vanderbilt-DeVita-Payne) =-99 Fermi-Dirac function Default: 0

title: degauss
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: gaussian broadening, Ry (not eV!) (see below)

title: Emin, Emax
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: min, max energy (eV) for DOS plot. If unspecified, the lower and/or upper band value, plus/minus 3 times the value of the gaussian smearing if present, will be used. Default: band extrema

title: DeltaE
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: energy grid step (eV)

title: fildos
subtitle: dos.x · &DOS
text: output file containing DOS(E) Default: 'prefix.dos'

title: dynmat.x
subtitle: Input reference · PHonon
text: Introduction Purpose of dynmat.x: - reads a dynamical matrix file produced by the phonon code - adds the non-analytical part (if Z* and epsilon are read from file), applies the chosen Acoustic Sum Rule (if q=0) - diagonalise the dynamical matrix - calculates IR and Raman cross sections (if Z* and Raman tensors are read from file, respectively) - writes the results to files, both for inspection and for plotting Structure of the input data: ======================================================================== &INPUT ...specs of namelist variables... /

title: fildyn
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: input file containing the dynamical matrix Default: 'matdyn'

title: q(i), i=1,3
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: calculate LO modes (add non-analytic terms) along the direction q (Cartesian axis) Default: q = (0,0,0)

title: amass(i), i=1,ntyp
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: mass for each atom type Default: amass is read from file fildyn

title: asr
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: Indicates the type of Acoustic Sum Rule imposed. Allowed values: 'no' no Acoustic Sum Rules imposed (default) 'simple' previous implementation of the asr used (3 translational asr imposed by correction of the diagonal elements of the dynamical matrix) 'crystal' 3 translational asr imposed by optimized correction of the dyn. matrix (projection) 'one-dim' 3 translational asr + 1 rotational asr imposed by optimized correction of the dyn. mat. (the rotation axis is the direction of periodicity; it will work only if this axis considered is one of the Cartesian axis). 'zero-dim' 3 translational asr + 3 rotational asr imposed by optimized correction of the dyn. mat. Note that in certain cases, not all the rotational asr can be applied (e.g. if there are only 2 atoms in a molecule or if all the atoms are aligned, etc.). In these cases the supplementary asr are canceled during the orthonormalization procedure (see below). Finally, in all cases except 'no' a simple correction on the effective charges is performed (same as in the previous implementation). Default: 'no' 'no' 'simple' 'crystal' 'one-dim' 'zero-dim'

title: remove_interaction_blocks
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: If .true. lines and rows corresponding to atoms that are not displaced are set to 0. This can be used for ph.x calculations with nat_todo set in ph.x, to remove the interaction between the diplaced and fixed parts of the system. Default: .false.

title: axis
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: indicates the rotation axis for a 1D system (1=Ox, 2=Oy, 3=Oz) Default: 3

title: lperm
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. then calculate Gamma-point mode contributions to dielectric permittivity tensor Default: .false.

title: lplasma
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. then calculate Gamma-point mode effective plasma frequencies, automatically triggers lperm = .true. Default: .false.

title: filout
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: output file containing phonon frequencies and normalized phonon displacements (i.e. eigenvectors divided by the square root of the mass and then normalized; they are not orthogonal) Default: 'dynmat.out'

title: fileig
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: output file containing phonon frequencies and eigenvectors of the dynamical matrix (they are orthogonal) Default: ' '

title: filmol
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: as above, in a format suitable for molden Default: 'dynmat.mold'

title: filxsf
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: as above, in axsf format suitable for xcrysden Default: 'dynmat.axsf'

title: loto_2d
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: set to .true. to activate two-dimensional treatment of LO-TO splitting. Default: '.false.'

title: el_ph_nsig
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: The number of double-delta smearing values used in an electron-phonon coupling calculation.

title: el_ph_sigma
subtitle: dynmat.x · &INPUT
text: The spacing of double-delta smearing values used in an electron-phonon coupling calculation.

title: turbo_davidson.x
subtitle: Input reference · turboTDDFPT
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends. All quantities whose dimensions are not explicitly specified are in RYDBERG ATOMIC UNITS BEWARE: TABS, DOS <CR><LF> CHARACTERS ARE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF TROUBLE Comment lines in namelists can be introduced by a "!", exactly as in fortran code. Comments lines in ``cards'' can be introduced by either a "!" or a "#" character in the first position of a line. Structure of the input data: =============================================================================== &LR_INPUT ... / &LR_DAV ... /

title: prefix
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Sets the prefix for generated and read files. The files generated by the ground state pw.x run should have this same prefix. Default: 'pwscf'

title: outdir
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The directory that contains the run critical files, which include the files generated by ground state pw.x run. Default: './'

title: wfcdir
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The directory that contains the run critical files, which include the files generated by ground state pw.x run. Default: './'

title: max_seconds
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: jobs stops after max_seconds CPU time. Use this option in conjunction with option restart if you need to split a job too long to complete into shorter jobs that fit into your batch queues. Default: 1.D+7, or 150 days, i.e. no time limit

title: restart
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: When set to .true., turbo_davidson.x will attempt to restart from a previous interrupted calculation if max_seconds was specified. Beware, if set to .false. turbo_davidson.x will OVERWRITE any previous runs. Default: .false.

title: lr_verbosity
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: This integer variable controls the amount of information written to standard output. Default: 1

title: disk_io
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Fine control of disk usage. Currently only 'reduced' is supported where no restart files are written, apart from the 'default' mode. Default: 'default'

title: num_eign
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Number of eigenstates to be calculated. Default: 1

title: num_init
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Number of trial vectors. Usually it is twice as large as the number of eigenstates to be calculated (see num_eign). Default: 2

title: if_random_init
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. trial vectors are chosen randomly, otherwise they are guessed from the ground-state calculation. If p_nbnd_occ * p_nbnd_virt < num_init, this term is forced to be .true. The usage of random trial vectors should cause only a slower convergence, and do not affect the final results. Default: .false.

title: num_basis_max
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Maximum number of basis vectors allowed in the subspace. When this number is reached, a discharging routine is called. The memory requirement of the Davidson algorithm is mainly determined by this variable (an estimation of the memory is reported at the beginning of the run). Default: 20

title: residue_conv_thr
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Threshold for the convergence. When the square of the residue is smaller than this value, the convergence is achieved. Default: 1.0E-4

title: precondition
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: If set to .true. a precondition is used. At this moment, one sees no reason why not to use the precondition. Default: .true.

title: single_pole
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: A slightly better way to set the initial trial vectors, but the improvement is really small. Currently this flag can be used only with LDA/PBE + NC PPs. So do not use it unless it is really necessary. Default: .false.

title: if_dft_spectrum
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. the independent particle approximation is used, i.e. the Hartree and exchange-correlation response contributions are neglected. Default: .false.

title: reference
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Reference energy in units of Ry. This variable is used to constrain the Davidson algorithm to converge the eigenstates having the energy closest to the reference energy. In this way one can calculate less eigenstates at once, and to perform multiple calculations with different reference energies (the post-processing code tddfpt_calculate_spectrum.x can be used for this purpose). Default: 0.0d0

title: broadening
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Lorentzian broadening (Ry) to broaden the absorption spectrum. Default: 0.005d0

title: start
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: The lower limit of the energy (Ry) scale for the spectrum calculation. Default: 0.0d0

title: finish
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: The upper limit of the energy (Ry) scale for the spectrum calculation. Default: 1.0d0

title: step
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Energy step (Ry) for the spectrum calculation. Default: 0.001d0

title: p_nbnd_occ
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Number of occupied states selected from the total number of occupied states computed by PWscf. This variable is useful if there are too many occupied states but your are interested in only some of them. In priciple this variable and p_nbnd_virt affect only the interpretation of the eigenstates, but do not effect their energy and the final absorption spectrum. Make sure that min(p_nbnd_occ,nbnd_occ)*min(p_nbnd_virt,nbnd_virt) is lager than the number of initial vectors (num_init), so you will not end up using random trial vectors which would slow down the convergence. Default: 10

title: p_nbnd_virt
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Number of empty states selected from the total number of empty states computed by PWscf. This variable is useful if there are too many empty states but your are interested in only some of them. In priciple this variable and p_nbnd_occ affect only the interpretation of the eigenstates, but do not effect their energy and the final absorption spectrum. Make sure that min(p_nbnd_occ,nbnd_occ)*min(p_nbnd_virt,nbnd_virt) is lager than the number of initial vectors (num_init), so you will not end up using random trial vectors which would slow down the convergence. Default: 10

title: poor_of_ram
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Use this variable if you do not have enough RAM (only USPP), i.e. set it to .true. When this variable is set to .false., you double the memory used for the USPP calculation, but you increase a speed of the calculation by getting rid of applying many times of s_psi and cal_bec in the calculation, which takes a lot of time (sometimes more than a half of the whole calculation) when the size of the subspace is more than 100. Default: .false.

title: poor_of_ram2
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Use this variable if you do not have enough RAM (NCPP and USPP), i.e. set it to .true. When this variable is set to .false., you double the memory used for the calculation, but you increase a speed of the calculation by storing D_ and C_ basis: the calculation will be speeded up a lot when one is calculating many transitions at the same time. Default: .false.

title: max_iter
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: Maximum number of Davidson iterations allowed. When the number of iterations arrives this number, the calculation will stop even if the convergence has not been achieved. Default: 100

title: no_hxc
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. the change in the internal field (Hartree and exchange-correlation) is ignored in the calculation, resulting in the independent electron approximation. Default: .false.

title: pseudo_hermitian
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. the pseudo-Hermitian Lanczos algorithm is used. When set to .false. the non-Hermitian Lanczos biorthogonalization algorithm is used (which is two times slower). Default: .true.

title: ltammd
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. the Tamm-Dancoff approximation is used in constructing the Liouvillian. Default: .false.

title: lplot_drho
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. the turbo_davidson.x code will write files for each eigenstate "drho-of-eign-$i" which are needed to plot the response charge-density at each resonance. This implies a calculation using the pp.x post-processing program with the corresponding input file which must be prepared. See example "H2O-PLOTRHO". Default: .false.

title: d0psi_rs
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: When set to .true. the dipole is computed in the real space. When set to .false. the dipole is computed in the reciprocal space by computing [H,r]. Note, currently the commutator does not contain a contribution for hybrids [V_EXX,r]. See also the variable lshift_d0psi. Important: Treatment of the dipole in the real space is allowed only if the system is finite. Default: .false.

title: lshift_d0psi
subtitle: turbo_davidson.x · &LR_DAV
text: This variable is used only when d0psi_rs = .true. a) If a molecule is placed in the corner of the supercell, there is a discontinuity problem for the position operator r, which is not periodic. By setting lshift_d0psi = .true. the discontinuity problem is solved by shifting the position operator r such that it is continuous and well defined. b) If a molecule is placed in the center of the supercell, there is no discontinuity problem for the position operator r, and thus you can set lshift_d0psi = .false. But if you still set it to .true., this will not harm, because the position operator will basically remain as it is, since it is always centered wrt the center of the molecule. Default: .true.

title: turbo_eels.x
subtitle: Input reference · turboEELS
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends. All quantities whose dimensions are not explicitly specified are in RYDBERG ATOMIC UNITS BEWARE: TABS, DOS <CR><LF> CHARACTERS ARE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF TROUBLE Comment lines in namelists can be introduced by a "!", exactly as in fortran code. Comments lines in ``cards'' can be introduced by either a "!" or a "#" character in the first position of a line. Structure of the input data: =============================================================================== &LR_INPUT ... / &LR_CONTROL ... /

title: prefix
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Sets the prefix for generated and read files. The files generated by the ground state pw.x run must have this same prefix. Default: 'pwscf'

title: outdir
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The directory that contains the run critical files, which include the files generated by ground state pw.x run. Default: './'

title: restart
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_INPUT
text: When set to .true., turbo_eels.x will attempt to restart from a previous interrupted calculation. (see restart_step variable). Beware, if set to .false. turbo_eels.x will OVERWRITE any previous runs. Default: .false.

title: restart_step
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The code writes restart files every restart_step iterations. Restart files are automatically written at the end of itermax Lanczos steps. Default: itermax

title: lr_verbosity
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_INPUT
text: This integer variable controls the amount of information written to standard output. Default: 1

title: disk_io
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Fine control of disk usage. Currently only 'reduced' is supported where no restart files are written, apart from the 'default' mode. Default: 'default'

title: approximation
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: A string describing a level of theory: 'TDDFT' Time-Dependent Local Density Approximation or Time-Dependent Generalized Gradient Approximation (depending on the XC functional) 'IPA' Independent Particle Approximation (IPA) 'RPA_with_CLFE' Random Phase Approximation (RPA) with Crystal Local Field Effects (CLFE) Default: 'TDDFT' 'TDDFT' 'IPA' 'RPA_with_CLFE'

title: q1, q2, q3
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: The values of the transferred momentum q = (q1, q2, q3) in Cartesian coordinates in units of 2pi/a, where "a" is the lattice parameter. Default: 1.0, 1.0, 1.0

title: calculator
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: Variable that controls which algorithm is used to compute EELS spectra. 'lanczos' corresponds to the Lanczos recursive algorithm 'sternheimer' corresponds to the Sternheimer algorithm Default: 'lanczos' 'lanczos' 'sternheimer'

title: itermax
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When calculator = 'lanczos', itermax is the maximum number of Lanczos iterations that will be performed. When calculator = 'sternheimer', itermax is the maximum number of iterations in a SCF step for each frequency. Default: 500

title: pseudo_hermitian
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'lanczos'. When set to .true. the pseudo-Hermitian Lanczos algorithm is used. When set to .false. the non-Hermitian Lanczos biorthogonalization algorithm is used (which is two times slower). Default: .true.

title: alpha_mix(i)
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'sternheimer'. Mixing parameter (for the i-th iteration) for updating the response SCF potential using the modified Broyden method: D.D. Johnson, PRB 38, 12807 (1988). Default: alpha_mix(1)=0.7

title: epsil
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'sternheimer'. The broadening/damping term (in Rydberg units). Default: 0.02

title: units
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'sternheimer'. The unit system used for the output, for start, end, and increment input parameters. 0 = Rydbergs, 1 = Electron volts. Default: 0

title: start
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'sternheimer'. start is the value of frequency starting from which the susceptibility and the loss function (-Im(1/eps)) will be computed. start is specified in units controlled by units. Default: 0.0

title: end
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'sternheimer'. end is the value of frequency up to which the susceptibility and the loss function (-Im(1/eps)) will be computed. end is specified in units controlled by units. Default: 2.5

title: increment
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when calculator = 'sternheimer'. increment is an incremental step used to define the mesh of frequencies between start and end. increment is specified in units controlled by units. Default: 0.001

title: ethr_nscf
subtitle: turbo_eels.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: Threshold for the convergence of eigenvalues during the iterative diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in the non-self-consistent-field (NSCF) calculation at k and k+q points. Note, this quantity is NOT extensive. Default: 1.D-11

title: hp.x
subtitle: Input reference · PWscf
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends, # = comment Structure of the input data: =============================================================================== &INPUTHP ... /

title: prefix
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Prepended to input/output filenames; must be the same used in the calculation of unperturbed system. Default: 'pwscf'

title: outdir
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Directory containing input, output, and scratch files; must be the same as specified in the calculation of the unperturbed system. Default: value of the ESPRESSO_TMPDIR environment variable if set; current directory ('./') otherwise

title: iverbosity
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: = 1 : minimal output = 2 : as above + symmetry matrices, final response matrices chi0 and chi1 and their inverse matrices, full U matrix = 3 : as above + various detailed info about the NSCF calculation at k and k+q = 4 : as above + response occupation matrices at every iteration and for every q point in the star Default: 1

title: max_seconds
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Maximum allowed run time before the job stops smoothly. Default: 1.d7

title: nq1, nq2, nq3
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Parameters of the Monkhorst-Pack grid (no offset). Same meaning as for nk1, nk2, nk3 in the input of pw.x. Default: 1,1,1

title: skip_equivalence_q
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If .true. then the HP code will skip the equivalence analysis of q points, and thus the full grid of q points will be used. Otherwise the symmetry is used to determine equivalent q points (star of q), and then perform calculations only for inequivalent q points. Default: .false.

title: determine_num_pert_only
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If .true. determines the number of perturbations (i.e. which atoms will be perturbed) and exits smoothly without performing any calculation. For DFT+U+V, it also determines the indices of inter-site couples. Default: .false.

title: determine_q_mesh_only
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If .true. determines the number of q points for a given perturbed atom and exits smoothly. This keyword can be used only if perturb_only_atom is set to .true. Default: .false.

title: find_atpert
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Method for searching of atoms which must be perturbed. 1 = Find how many inequivalent Hubbard atoms there are by analyzing unperturbed occupations. 2 = Find how many Hubbard atoms to perturb based on how many different Hubbard atomic types there are. Warning: atoms which have the same type but which are inequivalent by symmetry or which have different occupations will not be distinguished in this case (use option 1 or 3 instead). 3 = Find how many inequivalent Hubbard atoms there are using symmetry. Atoms which have the same type but are not equivalent by symmetry will be distinguished in this case. 4 = Perturb all Hubbard atoms (the most expensive option) Default: 1

title: docc_thr
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Threshold for a comparison of unperturbed occupations which is needed for the selection of atoms which must be perturbed. Can be used only when find_atpert = 1. Default: 5.D-5

title: skip_type(i), i=1,ntyp
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: skip_type(i), where i runs over types of atoms. If skip_type(i)=.true. then no linear-response calculation will be performed for the i-th atomic type: in this case equiv_type(i) must be specified, otherwise the HP code will stop. This option is useful if the system has atoms of the same type but opposite spin pollarizations (anti-ferromagnetic case). This keyword cannot be used when find_atpert = 1. Default: skip_type(i) = .false.

title: equiv_type(i), i=1,ntyp
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: equiv_type(i), where i runs over types of atoms. equiv_type(i)=j, will make type i equivalent to type j (useful when nspin=2). Such a merging of types is done only at the post-processing stage. This keyword cannot be used when find_atpert = 1. Default: equiv_type(i) = 0

title: perturb_only_atom(i), i=1,ntyp
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If perturb_only_atom(i)=.true. then only the i-th atom will be perturbed and considered in the run. This variable is useful when one wants to split the whole calculation on parts. Note: this variable has a higher priority than skip_type. Default: perturb_only_atom(i) = .false.

title: start_q
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Computes only the q points from start_q to last_q. IMPORTANT: start_q must be smaller or equal to the total number of q points found. Default: 1

title: last_q
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Computes only the q points from start_q to last_q. IMPORTANT: last_q must be smaller or equal to the total number of q points found. Default: number of q points

title: sum_pertq
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If it is set to .true. then the HP code will collect pieces of the response occupation matrices for all q points. This variable should be used only when start_q, last_q and perturb_only_atom are used. Default: .false.

title: compute_hp
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If it is set to .true. then the HP code will collect pieces of the chi0 and chi matrices (which must have been produced in previous runs) and then compute Hubbard parameters. The HP code will look for files tmp_dir/HP/prefix.chi.i.dat. Note that all files prefix.chi.i.dat (where i runs over all perturbed atoms) must be placed in one folder tmp_dir/HP/. compute_hp=.true. must be used only when the calculation was parallelized over perturbations. Default: .false.

title: conv_thr_chi
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Convergence threshold for the response function chi, which is defined as a trace of the response occupation matrix. Default: 1.D-5

title: thresh_init
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Initial threshold for the solution of the linear system (first iteration). Needed to converge the bare (non-interacting) response function chi0. The specified value will be multiplied by the number of electrons in the system. Default: 1.D-14

title: ethr_nscf
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Threshold for the convergence of eigenvalues during the iterative diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in the non-self-consistent-field (NSCF) calculation at k and k+q points. Note, this quantity is NOT extensive. Default: 1.D-11

title: niter_max
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Maximum number of iterations in the iterative solution of the linear-response Kohn-Sham equations. Default: 100

title: alpha_mix(i)
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Mixing parameter (for the i-th iteration) for updating the response SCF potential using the modified Broyden method. See: D.D. Johnson, PRB 38, 12807 (1988). Default: alpha_mix(1)=0.3

title: nmix
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Number of iterations used in potential mixing using the modified Broyden method. See: D.D. Johnson, PRB 38, 12807 (1988). Default: 4

title: num_neigh
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Number of nearest neighbors of every Hubbard atom which will be considered when writting Hubbard V parameters to the file parameters.out, which can be used in the subsequent DFT+U+V calculation. This keyword is used only for DFT+U+V (post-processing stage). Default: 6

title: lmin
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Minimum value of the orbital quantum number of the Hubbard atoms starting from which (and up to the maximum l in the system) Hubbard V will be written to the file parameters.out. lmin refers to the orbital quantum number of the atom corresponding to the first site-index in Hubbard_V(:,:,:). This keyword is used only for DFT+U+V and only in the post-processing stage. Example: lmin=1 corresponds to writing to file V between e.g. oxygen (with p states) and its neighbors, and including V between transition metals (with d states) and their neighbors. Instead, when lmin=2 only the latter will be written to parameters.out. Default: 2

title: rmax
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Maximum distance (in Bohr) between two atoms to search neighbors (used only at the postprocessing step for DFT+U+V). This keyword is useful when there are e.g. defects in the system. Default: 100.D0

title: dist_thr
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: Threshold (in Bohr) for comparing inter-atomic distances when reconstructing the missing elements of the response susceptibility in the post-processing step. Default: 6.D-4

title: no_metq0
subtitle: hp.x · &INPUTHP
text: If .true. the metallic response term at q=0 is ignored (i.e. the last term in Eq. (22) in PRB 103, 045141 (2021)). This is useful for magnetic insulators to avoid the divergence of the calculation. Default: .false.

title: ld1.x
subtitle: Input reference
text: Introduction Input data cards for ld1.x program: Always present: 1 namelist &input 1.1 optional cards for all-electron calculations Needed for PP generation: 2 namelist &inputp 2.1 additional cards for PP generation Needed for pseudo-potential (PP) test. optional for PP generation: 3 namelist &test 3.1 optional cards for PP test

title: title
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: A string describing the job.

title: zed
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: The nuclear charge (1 < zed < 100). IMPORTANT: Specify either zed OR atom, not both!

title: atom
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Atomic symbol: atom='H', 'He', 'Be', etc. IMPORTANT: Specify either atom OR zed, not both!

title: xmin
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Radial grid parameter. Default: -7.0 if iswitch>1 or rel=0, -8.0 otherwise

title: dx
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Radial grid parameter. The radial grid is: r(i+1) = exp(xmin+i*dx)/zed a.u. Default: 0.0125 if iswitch>1, 0.008 otherwise

title: rmax
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Outermost grid point. Default: 100.0 a.u.

title: beta
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: parameter for potential mixing Default: 0.2

title: tr2
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: convergence threshold for scf Default: 1e-14

title: iswitch
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 1 all-electron calculation 2 PP test calculation 3 PP generation 4 LDA-1/2 correction, needs a previously generated PP file Default: 1

title: nld
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: the number of logarithmic derivatives to be calculated

title: rlderiv
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: radius (a.u.) at which logarithmic derivatives are calculated

title: eminld, emaxld
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Energy range (min, max energy, in Ry) at which logarithmic derivatives are calculated.

title: deld
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Delta e (Ry) of energy for logarithmic derivatives.

title: rpwe
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: radius (a.u.) at which partial wave expansions are calculated Default: rlderiv

title: rel
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 0 ... non relativistic calculation 1 ... scalar relativistic calculation 2 ... full relativistic calculation with spin-orbit Default: 0 for Z <= 18; 1 for Z > 18

title: lsmall
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. writes on files the small component Default: .false.

title: max_out_wfc
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Maximum number of atomic wavefunctions written in the output file. Default: 7

title: noscf
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. the charge is not computed. The occupations are not used and the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions are those of a hydrogen-like atom. Default: .false.

title: lsd
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 0 ... non spin polarized calculation 1 ... spin-polarized calculation BEWARE: not allowed if iswitch=3 (PP generation) or with full relativistic calculation Default: 0

title: dft
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Exchange-correlation functional. Examples: 'PZ' Perdew and Zunger formula for LDA 'PW91' Perdew and Wang GGA 'BP' Becke and Perdew GGA 'PBE' Perdew, Becke and Ernzerhof GGA 'BLYP' ... For the complete list, see module "functionals" in ../Modules/ The default is 'PZ' for all-electron calculations, it is read from the PP file in a PP calculation.

title: latt
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 0 ... no Latter correction 1 ... apply Latter correction Default: 0

title: isic
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 0 ... no Self-interaction correction 1 ... apply Self-interaction correction Default: 0

title: rytoev_fact
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Factor used to convert Ry into eV. Default: as specified in file Modules/constants.f90

title: cau_fact
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Speed of light in a.u.. (Be careful the default value is always used in the relativistic exchange.) Default: as specified in file Modules/constants.f90

title: vdw
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: If .true., the frequency dependent polarizability and van der Waals coefficient C6 will be computed in Thomas-Fermi and von Weizsaecker approximation(only for closed-shell ions). Default: .false.

title: prefix
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Prefix for file names - only for output file names containing the orbitals, logarithmic derivatives, tests See below for file names and the content of the file. Default: 'ld1'

title: verbosity
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 'low' or 'high' if 'high' with iswitch=2,3 prints separately core and valence contributions to the energies. Print the frozen-core energy. Default: 'low'

title: file_charge
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: Name of the file where the code writes the all-electron total charge. No charge is written if file_charge=' '. Default: ' '

title: config
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: A string with the electronic configuration. Example: '[Ar] 3d10 4s2 4p2.5' * If lsd=1, spin-up and spin-down state may appear twice with the respective occupancy: 3p4 3p2 = 4 up, 2 down. Otherwise, the Hund's rule is assumed. * If rel=2, states with jj=l-1/2 are filled first. If a state appears twice, the first one has jj=l-1/2, the second one jj=l+1/2 (except S states) (Use rel_dist if you want to average the electrons over all available states.) * If config='default' the code uses zed to set the ground state electronic configuration for the atom. Negative occupancies are used to flag unbound states; they are not actually used. Default: ' '

title: relpert
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: If .true. the relativistic corrections to the non-relativistic Kohn-Sham energy levels (rel=0 .and. lsd=0) are computed using first-order perturbation theory in all-electron calculations. The corrections consist of the following terms: E_vel: velocity (p^4) correction E_Dar: Darwin term E_S-O: spin-orbit coupling The spin-orbit term vanishes for s-electron states and gives rise to a splitting of (2*l+1)*E_S-O for the other states. The separate contributions are printed only if verbosity='high'. Formulas and notation are based on the Herman-Skillman book: F. Herman and S. Skillman, "Atomic Structure Calculations", Prentice-Hall, Inc., Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey, 1963 Default: .false.

title: rel_dist
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: 'energy' or 'average' * if 'energy' the relativistic l-1/2 states are filled first. * if 'average' the electrons are uniformly distributed among all the states with the given l. Default: 'energy'

title: write_coulomb
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUT
text: If .true., a fake pseudo-potential file with name X.UPF, where X is the atomic symbol, is written. It contains the radial grid and the wavefunctions as specified in input, plus the info needed to build the Coulomb potential for an all-electron calculation - for testing only. Default: .false.

title: nwf
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: number of wavefunctions

title: nl
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: wavefunction label (e.g. 1s, 2s, etc.)

title: n
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: principal quantum number

title: l
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: angular quantum number

title: oc
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: occupation number

title: isw
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: the spin index (1-2) used only in the lsda case

title: jj
subtitle: ld1.x · AllElectronCards
text: The total angular momentum (0.0 is allowed for complete shells: the codes fills 2l states with jj=l-1/2, 2l+2 with jj=l+1/2).

title: zval
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Valence charge. zval is automatically calculated from available data. If the value of zval is provided in input, it will be checked versus the calculated value. The only case in which you need to explicitly provide the value of zval for noninteger zval (i.e. half core-hole pseudo-potentials). Default: (calculated)

title: pseudotype
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: 1 ... norm-conserving, single-projector PP IMPORTANT: if pseudotype=1 all calculations are done using the SEMILOCAL form, not the separable nonlocal form 2 ... norm-conserving PP in separable form (obsolescent) All calculations are done using SEPARABLE non-local form IMPORTANT: multiple projectors allowed but not properly implemented, use only if you know what you are doing 3 ... ultrasoft PP or PAW

title: file_pseudopw
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: File where the generated PP is written. * if the file name ends with "upf" or "UPF", or in any case for spin-orbit PP (rel=2), the file is written in UPF format; * if the file name ends with 'psp' it is written in native CPMD format (this is currently an experimental feature); otherwise it is written in the old "NC" format if pseudotype=1, or in the old RRKJ format if pseudotype=2 or 3 (no default, must be specified).

title: file_recon
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: File containing data needed for GIPAW reconstruction of all-electron wavefunctions from PP results. If you want to use additional states to perform the reconstruction, add them at the end of the list of all-electron states. Default: ' '

title: lloc
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Angular momentum of the local channel. * lloc=-1 or lloc=-2 pseudizes the all-electron potential if lloc=-2 the original recipe of Troullier-Martins is used (zero first and second derivatives at r=0) * lloc>-1 uses the corresponding channel as local PP NB: if lloc>-1, the corresponding channel must be the last in the list of wavefunctions appearing after the namelist &inputp In the relativistic case, if lloc > 0 both the j=lloc-1/2 and the j=lloc+1/2 wavefunctions must be at the end of the list. Default: -1

title: rcloc
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Matching radius (a.u.) for local pseudo-potential (no default).

title: nlcc
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: If .true. produce a PP with the nonlinear core correction of Louie, Froyen, and Cohen [PRB 26, 1738 (1982)]. Default: .false.

title: new_core_ps
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: If .true. pseudizes the core charge with bessel functions. Default: .false.

title: rcore
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Matching radius (a.u.) for the smoothing of the core charge. If not specified, the matching radius is determined by the condition: rho_core(rcore) = 2*rho_valence(rcore)

title: tm
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: * .true. for Troullier-Martins pseudization [PRB 43, 1993 (1991)] * .false. for Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos pseudization [PRB 41, 1227 (1990), erratum PRB 44, 13175 (1991)] Default: .false.

title: rho0
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Charge at the origin: when the Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos method with 3 Bessel functions fails, specifying rho0 > 0 may allow to override the problem (using 4 Bessel functions). Typical values are in the order of 0.01-0.02 Default: 0.0

title: lpaw
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: If .true. produce a PAW dataset, experimental feature only for pseudotype=3 Default: .false.

title: which_augfun
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: If different from 'AE' the augmentation functions are pseudized before rmatch_augfun. The pseudization options are: * 'PSQ' Use Bessel functions to pseudize Q from the origin to rmatch_augfun. These features are available only for PAW: * 'BESSEL' Use Bessel functions to pseudize the Q. * 'GAUSS' Use 2 Gaussian functions to pseudize the Q. * 'BG' Use original Bloechl's recipe with a single gaussian. Note: if lpaw is true and which_augfun is set to AE real all- electron charge will be used, which will produce extremely hard augmentation. Default: 'AE' for Vanderbilt-Ultrasoft pseudo-potentials and 'BESSEL' for PAW datasets.

title: rmatch_augfun
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Pseudization radius for the augmentation functions. Presently it has the same value for all L. Default: 0.5 a.u.

title: rmatch_augfun_nc
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: If .true. the augmentation functions are pseudized from the origin to min(rcut(ns),rcut(ns1)) where ns and ns1 are the two channels for that Q. In this case rmatch_augfun is not used. Default: .false.

title: lsave_wfc
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Set it to .true. to save all-electron and pseudo wavefunctions used in the pseudo-potential generation in the UPF file. Only works for UPFv2 format. Default: .false. if .not. lpaw, otherwise .true.

title: lgipaw_reconstruction
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Set it to .true. to generate pseudo-potentials containing the additional info required for reconstruction of all-electron orbitals, used by GIPAW. You will typically need to specify additional projectors beyond those used in the generation of pseudo-potentials. You should also specify file_recon. All projectors used in the reconstruction must be listed BOTH in the test configuration after namelist &test AND in the all-electron configuration (variable 'config', namelist &inputp, Use negative occupancies for projectors on unbound states). The core radii in the test configuration should be the same as in the pseudo-potential generation section and will be used as the radius of reconstruction. Projectors not used to generate the pseudo-potential should have zero occupation number. Default: .false.

title: use_paw_as_gipaw
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: When generating a PAW dataset, setting this option to .true. will save the core all-electron wavefunctions to the UPF file. The GIPAW reconstruction to be performed using the PAW data and projectors for the valence wavefunctions. In the default case, the GIPAW valence wavefunction and projectors are independent from the PAW ones and must be then specified as explained above in lgipaw_reconstruction. Setting this to .true. always implies lgipaw_reconstruction = .true. Default: .false.

title: author
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: Name of the author. Default: 'anonymous'

title: file_chi
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file containing output PP chi functions Default: ' '

title: file_beta
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file containing output PP beta functions Default: ' '

title: file_qvan
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file containing output PP qvan functions Default: ' '

title: file_screen
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file containing output screening potential Default: ' '

title: file_core
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file containing output total and core charge Default: ' '

title: file_wfcaegen
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file with the all-electron wfc for generation Default: ' '

title: file_wfcncgen
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file with the norm-conserving wfc for generation Default: ' '

title: file_wfcusgen
subtitle: ld1.x · &INPUTP
text: file with the ultra-soft wfc for generation Default: ' '

title: nwfs
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: number of wavefunctions to be pseudized

title: nls
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Wavefunction label (same as in the all-electron configuration).

title: nns
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Principal quantum number (referred to the PSEUDOPOTENTIAL case; nns=1 for lowest s, nns=2 for lowest p, and so on).

title: lls
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Angular momentum quantum number.

title: ocs
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Occupation number (same as in the all-electron configuration).

title: ener
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Energy (Ry) used to pseudize the corresponding state. If 0.d0, use the one-electron energy of the all-electron state. Do not use 0.d0 for unbound states!

title: rcut
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Matching radius (a.u.) for norm conserving PP.

title: rcutus
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: Matching radius (a.u.) for ultrasoft PP - only for pseudotype=3.

title: jjs
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialGenerationCards
text: The total angular momentum (0.0 is allowed for complete shells).

title: nconf
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: the number of configurations to be tested. For iswitch=4 nconf=2 Default: 1

title: file_pseudo
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: File containing the PP. * If the file name contains ".upf" or ".UPF", the file is assumed to be in UPF format; * else if the file name contains ".rrkj3" or ".RRKJ3", the old RRKJ format is first tried; * otherwise, the old NC format is read. IMPORTANT: in the latter case, all calculations are done using the SEMILOCAL form, not the separable nonlocal form. Use the UPF format if you want to test the separable form! Default: ' '

title: ecutmin, ecutmax, decut
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: Parameters (Ry) used for test with a basis set of spherical Bessel functions j_l(qr) . The hamiltonian at fixed scf potential is diagonalized for various values of ecut: ecutmin, ecutmin+decut, ecutmin+2*decut ... up to ecutmax. This yields an indication of convergence with the corresponding plane-wave cutoff in solids, and shows in an unambiguous way if there are "ghost" states Default: decut=5.0 Ry; ecutmin=ecutmax=0Ry

title: rm
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: Radius of the box used with spherical Bessel functions. Default: 30 a.u.

title: configts(i), i=1,nconf
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: A string array containing the test electronic configuration. configts(nc), nc=1,nconf, has the same syntax as for config but only VALENCE states must be included. If configts(i) is not set, the electron configuration is read from the cards following the namelist.

title: lsdts(i), i=1,nconf
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: 0 or 1. It is the value of lsd used in the i-th test. Allows to make simultaneously spin-polarized and spin-unpolarized tests. Default: 1

title: frozen_core
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: If .true. only the core wavefunctions of the first configuration are calculated. The eigenvalues, orbitals and energies of the other configurations are calculated with the core of the first configuration. The first configuration must be spin-unpolarized. Default: .false.

title: rcutv
subtitle: ld1.x · &TEST
text: Cutoff distance (CUT) for the inclusion of LDA-1/2 potential. Needed (mandatory) only if iswitch = 4 Default: -1.0

title: nwfts
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialTestCards
text: number of wavefunctions

title: iswts
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialTestCards
text: spin index (1 or 2, used in lsda case)

title: jjts
subtitle: ld1.x · PseudoPotentialTestCards
text: total angular momentum of the state

title: turbo_lanczos.x
subtitle: Input reference · turboTDDFPT
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends. All quantities whose dimensions are not explicitly specified are in RYDBERG ATOMIC UNITS BEWARE: TABS, DOS <CR><LF> CHARACTERS ARE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF TROUBLE Comment lines in namelists can be introduced by a "!", exactly as in fortran code. Comments lines in ``cards'' can be introduced by either a "!" or a "#" character in the first position of a line. Structure of the input data: =============================================================================== &LR_INPUT ... / &LR_CONTROL ... / [ &LR_POST ... / ]

title: prefix
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Sets the prefix for generated and read files. The files generated by the ground state pw.x run should have this same prefix. Default: 'pwscf'

title: outdir
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The directory that contains the run critical files, which include the files generated by ground state pw.x run. Default: './'

title: wfcdir
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The directory that contains the run critical files, which include the files generated by ground state pw.x run. Default: './'

title: restart
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: When set to .true., turbo_lanczos.x will attempt to restart from a previous interrupted calculation. (see restart_step variable). Beware, if set to .false. turbo_lanczos.x will OVERWRITE any previous runs. Default: .false.

title: restart_step
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The code writes restart files every restart_step iterations. Restart files are automatically written at the end of itermax Lanczos steps. Default: itermax

title: lr_verbosity
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: This integer variable controls the amount of information written to standard output. Default: 1

title: disk_io
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Fine control of disk usage. Currently only 'reduced' is supported where no restart files are written, apart from the 'default' mode. Default: 'default'

title: itermax
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: Number of Lanczos iterations to be performed. Default: 500

title: ipol
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: An integer variable that determines which element of the dynamical polarizability will be computed: 1 -> alpha_xx(omega), 2 -> alpha_yy(omega), and 3 -> alpha_zz(omega). When set to 4, three Lanczos chains are sequentially performed and the full polarizability tensor and the absorption coefficient are computed. Default: 1

title: n_ipol
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: Determines the number of zeta coefficients to be calculated for a given polarization direction. Default: 1 if ipol < 4; 3 if ipol=4

title: ltammd
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to .true. the Tamm-Dancoff approximation is used in constructing the Liouvillian. Default: .false.

title: no_hxc
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to .true. the change in the internal field (Hartree and exchange-correlation) is ignored in the calculation, resulting in the independent electron approximation. Default: .false.

title: lrpa
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to .true. the Random Phase Approximation is used (no exchange and correlation). Default: .false.

title: scissor
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: Scissor shift (in Rydberg units). Default: 0.0

title: charge_response
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to 1, the code computes the response of the charge density and writes it into a file format determined by the variable plot type. Setting charge response to 1 makes the presence of the card lr post mandatory. Default: 0

title: pseudo_hermitian
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to .true. the pseudo-Hermitian Lanczos algorithm is used. When set to .false. the non-Hermitian Lanczos biorthogonalization algorithm is used (which is two times slower). Default: .true.

title: d0psi_rs
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to .true. the dipole is computed in the real space. When set to .false. the dipole is computed in the reciprocal space by computing [H,r]. Note, currently the commutator does not contain a contribution for hybrids [V_EXX,r]. See also the variable lshift_d0psi. Important: Treatment of the dipole in the real space is allowed only if the system is finite. Default: .false.

title: lshift_d0psi
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: This variable is used only when d0psi_rs = .true. a) If a molecule is placed in the corner of the supercell, there is a discontinuity problem for the position operator r, which is not periodic. By setting lshift_d0psi=.true. the discontinuity problem is solved by shifting the position operator r such that it is continuous and well defined. b) If a molecule is placed in the center of the supercell, there is no discontinuity problem for the position operator r, and thus you can set lshift_d0psi=.false. But if you still set it to .true., this will not harm, because the position operator will basically remain as it is, since it is always centered wrt the center of the molecule. Default: .true.

title: omeg
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_POST
text: The response of the charge density is calculated for this transition energy (in Rydberg units) Default: 0.0

title: epsil
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_POST
text: The broadening/damping term (in Rydberg units). Default: 0.02

title: beta_gamma_z_prefix
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_POST
text: The prefix of the file where the beta gamma zeta coefficients from the first calculation can be set manually using this parameter. The file outdir/beta gamma z prefix.beta gamma z.x (where x=1-3) must exist. Default: 'pwscf'

title: w_T_npol
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_POST
text: Number of polarization directions considered in the previous calculation. It must be set to 3 if in the previous calculation ipol=4, it must be set to 1 otherwise. Default: 1

title: plot_type
subtitle: turbo_lanczos.x · &LR_POST
text: An integer variable that determines the format of the file containing the charge density response. 1: A file containing the x y z grid coordinates and the corre- sponding value of the density is produced 2: The density response is written in Xcrysden format 3: The density response is written in the gaussian cube format. Default: 1

title: matdyn.x
subtitle: Input reference · PHonon
text: Introduction Purpose of matdyn.x: This program calculates the phonon frequencies for a list of generic q vectors starting from the interatomic force constants generated from the dynamical matrices as written by DFPT phonon code through the companion program q2r.x matdyn.x can generate a supercell of the original cell for mass approximation calculation. If supercell data are not specified in input, the unit cell, lattice vectors, atom types and positions are read from the force constant file. Input data format: [ ] = it depends Structure of the input data: ======================================================================== &INPUT ...specs of the namelist variables... / [ X(1) Y(1) Z(1) ityp(1) ... X(nat) Y(nat) Z(nat) ityp(nat) ] [ nq q_x(1) q_y(1) q_x(1) [ nptq(1) ] ... q_x(nq) q_y(nq) q_x(nq) [ nptq(1) ] ]

title: flfrc
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: File produced by q2r containing force constants (needed) It is the same as in the input of q2r.x (+ the .xml extension if the dynamical matrices produced by ph.x were in xml format). No default value: must be specified.

title: asr
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: Indicates the type of Acoustic Sum Rule imposed. Allowed values: 'no' no Acoustic Sum Rules imposed (default) 'simple' previous implementation of the asr used (3 translational asr imposed by correction of the diagonal elements of the force constants matrix) 'crystal' 3 translational asr imposed by optimized correction of the force constants (projection) 'all' 3 translational asr + 3 rotational asr + 15 Huang conditions for vanishing stress tensor, imposed by optimized correction of the force constants (projection). Remember to set write_lr = .true. to write long-range force constants into file when running q2r and set read_lr = .true. when running matdyn in the case of infrared-active solids. (See npj Comput Mater 8, 236 (2022)) 'one-dim' 3 translational asr + 1 rotational asr imposed by optimized correction of the dyn. mat. (the rotation axis is the direction of periodicity; it will work only if this axis considered is one of the Cartesian axis). 'zero-dim' 3 translational asr + 3 rotational asr imposed by optimized correction of the dyn. mat. Note that in certain cases, not all the rotational asr can be applied (e.g. if there are only 2 atoms in a molecule or if all the atoms are aligned, etc.). In these cases the supplementary asr are cancelled during the orthonormalization procedure (see below). Default: 'no' 'no' 'simple' 'crystal' 'all' 'one-dim' 'zero-dim'

title: huang
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. 15 Huang conditions for vanishing stress tensor are included in asr = 'all'. Default: .true.

title: dos
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. calculate phonon Density of States (DOS) using tetrahedra and a uniform q-point grid (see below) NB: may not work properly in noncubic materials if .false. calculate phonon bands from the list of q-points supplied in input (default)

title: nk1, nk2, nk3
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: uniform q-point grid for DOS calculation (includes q=0) (must be specified if dos = .true., ignored otherwise)

title: deltaE
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: energy step, in cm-1, for DOS calculation: from min to max phonon energy (default: 1 cm-1 if ndos, see below, is not specified)

title: ndos
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: number of energy steps for DOS calculations (default: calculated from deltaE if not specified)

title: degauss
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: DOS broadening in cm-1 Default: 0 - meaning use tetrahedra

title: fldos
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: output file for dos (default: 'matdyn.dos') the dos is in states/cm-1 plotted vs omega in cm(-1) and is normalised to 3*nat, i.e. the number of phonons

title: flfrq
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: output file for frequencies (default: 'matdyn.freq')

title: flvec
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: output file for normalized phonon displacements (default: 'matdyn.modes'). The normalized phonon displacements are the eigenvectors divided by the square root of the mass, then normalized. As such they are not orthogonal.

title: fleig
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: output file for phonon eigenvectors (default: 'matdyn.eig') The phonon eigenvectors are the eigenvectors of the dynamical matrix. They are orthogonal.

title: fldyn
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: output file for dynamical matrix (default: ' ' i.e. not written)

title: at(i,j), (i,j) = (1,1) . . . (3,3)
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: supercell lattice vectors - must form a superlattice of the original lattice (default: use original cell)

title: l1, l2, l3
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: supercell lattice vectors are original cell vectors times l1, l2, l3 respectively (default: 1, ignored if at specified)

title: ntyp
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: number of atom types in the supercell (default: ntyp of the original cell)

title: amass(i), i=1,ntyp
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: masses of atoms in the supercell (a.m.u.), one per atom type (default: use masses read from file flfrc)

title: readtau
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: read atomic positions of the supercell from input (used to specify different masses) (default: .false.)

title: fltau
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: write atomic positions of the supercell to file fltau (default: fltau = ' ', do not write)

title: la2F
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. interpolates also the el-ph coefficients

title: q_in_band_form
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. the q points are given in band form: only the first and last point of one or more lines are given. See below. (default: .false.).

title: q_in_cryst_coord
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. input q points are in crystalline coordinates (default: .false.)

title: eigen_similarity
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: use similarity of the displacements to order frequencies (default: .false.) NB: You cannot use this option with the symmetry analysis of the modes.

title: fd
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. the ifc come from the finite displacement calculation

title: na_ifc
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: add non analitic contributions to the interatomic force constants if finite displacement method is used (as in Wang et al. PRB 85, 224303 (2012)) [to be used in conjunction with fd.x]

title: nosym
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true., no symmetry and no time reversal are imposed

title: loto_2d
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: set to .true. to activate two-dimensional treatment of LO-TO splitting

title: loto_disable
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. do not apply LO-TO splitting for q=0 (default: .false.)

title: read_lr
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. read also long-range force constants when they exist in force constant file. This is required when enforcing asr = 'all' for infrared-active solids. Default: .false.

title: write_frc
subtitle: matdyn.x · &INPUT
text: if .true. write force constants with asr imposed into file. The filename would be flfrc+".matdyn". The long-range part of force constants will be not written. Default: .false.

title: X, Y, Z
subtitle: matdyn.x · AtomicPositionSpecs
text: X, Y, Z atomic positions

title: ityp
subtitle: matdyn.x · AtomicPositionSpecs
text: index of the atomic type

title: nq
subtitle: matdyn.x · qPointsSpecs
text: number of q points

title: q_x, q_y, q_z
subtitle: matdyn.x · qPointsSpecs
text: coordinates of the Q point

title: nptq
subtitle: matdyn.x · qPointsSpecs
text: The number of points between this point and the next. nptq is the number of points between this point and the next. These points are automatically generated. the q points are given in Cartesian coordinates, 2pi/a units (a = lattice parameters)

title: nq
subtitle: matdyn.x · qPointsSpecs
text: number of q points

title: q_x, q_y, q_z
subtitle: matdyn.x · qPointsSpecs
text: q-points in cartesian coordinates, 2pi/a units (a = lattice parameters)

title: turbo_magnon.x
subtitle: Input reference · turboMAGNON
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends. All quantities whose dimensions are not explicitly specified are in RYDBERG ATOMIC UNITS BEWARE: TABS, DOS <CR><LF> CHARACTERS ARE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF TROUBLE Comment lines in namelists can be introduced by a "!", exactly as in fortran code. Comments lines in ``cards'' can be introduced by either a "!" or a "#" character in the first position of a line. Structure of the input data: =============================================================================== &LR_INPUT ... / &LR_CONTROL ... /

title: prefix
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Sets the prefix for generated and read files. The files generated by the ground state pw.x run must have this same prefix. Default: 'pwscf'

title: outdir
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The directory that contains the run critical files, which include the files generated by ground state pw.x run. Default: './'

title: restart
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_INPUT
text: When set to .true., turbo_magnons.x will attempt to restart from a previous interrupted calculation. (see restart_step variable). Beware, if set to .false. turbo_magnons.x will OVERWRITE any previous runs. Default: .false.

title: restart_step
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_INPUT
text: The code writes restart files every restart_step iterations. Restart files are automatically written at the end of itermax Lanczos steps. Default: itermax

title: lr_verbosity
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_INPUT
text: This integer variable controls the amount of information written to standard output. Default: 1

title: disk_io
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_INPUT
text: Fine control of disk usage. Currently only 'reduced' is supported where no restart files are written, apart from the 'default' mode. Default: 'default'

title: itermax
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: Number of Lanczos iterations to be performed. Default: 500

title: pseudo_hermitian
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: When set to .true. the pseudo-Hermitian Lanczos algorithm is used. When set to .false. the non-Hermitian Lanczos biorthogonalization algorithm is used (which is two times slower). Default: .true.

title: approximation
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: A string describing a level of theory: 'TDDFT' - Time-Dependent Local Density Approximation or Time-Dependent Generalized Gradient Approximation (depending on the XC functional), 'IPA' - Independent Particle Approximation, Default: 'TDDFT'

title: ipol
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: An integer variable that determines which column of the dynamical magnetic susceptibility will be computed: 1 -> chi_ax(omega), 2 -> chi_ay(omega), and 3 -> chi_az(omega), with a=(x,y,z). When set to 4, three Lanczos chains are sequentially performed and the full susceptibility tensor is computed. Default: 1

title: q1, q2, q3
subtitle: turbo_magnon.x · &LR_CONTROL
text: The values of the transferred momentum q = (q1, q2, q3) in Cartesian coordinates in units of 2pi/a, where "a" is the lattice parameter. Default: 1.0, 1.0, 1.0

title: neb.x
subtitle: Input reference · NEB
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends, | = or All quantities whose dimensions are not explicitly specified are in RYDBERG ATOMIC UNITS BEWARE: TABS, DOS <CR><LF> CHARACTERS ARE POTENTIAL SOURCES OF TROUBLE neb.x DOES NOT READ FROM STANDARD INPUT ! There are two ways for running a calculation with neb.x: (1) specifying a file to parse with the ./neb.x -inp or ./neb.x -input command line option. (2) or specifying the number of copies of PWscf inputs with the ./neb.x -input_images For case (1) a file containing special KEYWORDS (aka SUPERCARDS) has to be written (see below). These KEYWORDS tell the parser which part of the file contains the neb specifics and which part contains the energy/force engine input (at the moment only PW). After the parsing, different files are generated: neb.dat, with the neb specific variables, and a set of pw_*.in PWscf input files, i.e., one for each input position. All options for a single SCF calculation apply. The general structure of the file to be parsed is: ================================================== BEGIN BEGIN_PATH_INPUT ... neb specific namelists and cards END_PATH_INPUT BEGIN_ENGINE_INPUT ...pw specific namelists and cards BEGIN_POSITIONS FIRST_IMAGE ...pw ATOMIC_POSITIONS card ...pw TOTAL_CHARGE card (only for FCP) INTERMEDIATE_IMAGE ...pw ATOMIC_POSITIONS card ...pw TOTAL_CHARGE card (only for FCP) LAST_IMAGE ...pw ATOMIC_POSITIONS card ...pw TOTAL_CHARGE card (only for FCP) END_POSITIONS ... other pw specific cards END_ENGINE_INPUT END For case (2) neb.dat and all pw_1.in, pw_2.in ... should be already present. Structure of the NEB-only input data (file neb.dat): ==================================================== &PATH ... / [ CLIMBING_IMAGES list of images, separated by a comma ]

title: string_method
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: A string describing the task to be performed. Options are: 'neb' nudget-elastic-band 'smd' string-method-dynamics Default: 'neb' 'neb' 'smd'

title: restart_mode
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Options are: 'from_scratch' from scratch 'restart' from previous interrupted run Default: 'from_scratch' 'from_scratch' 'restart'

title: nstep_path
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: number of ionic + electronic steps Default: 1

title: num_of_images
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Number of points used to discretize the path (it must be larger than 3). Default: 0

title: opt_scheme
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Specify the type of optimization scheme: 'sd' steepest descent 'broyden' quasi-Newton Broyden's second method (suggested) 'broyden2' another variant of the quasi-Newton Broyden's second method to be tested and compared with the previous one. 'quick-min' an optimisation algorithm based on the projected velocity Verlet scheme 'langevin' finite temperature langevin dynamics of the string (smd only). It is used to compute the average path and the free-energy profile. Default: 'quick-min' 'sd' 'broyden' 'broyden2' 'quick-min' 'langevin'

title: CI_scheme
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Specify the type of Climbing Image scheme: 'no-CI' climbing image is not used 'auto' original CI scheme. The image highest in energy does not feel the effect of springs and is allowed to climb along the path 'manual' images that have to climb are manually selected. See also CLIMBING_IMAGES card Default: 'no-CI' 'no-CI' 'auto' 'manual'

title: first_last_opt
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Also the first and the last configurations are optimized "on the fly" (these images do not feel the effect of the springs). Default: .FALSE.

title: minimum_image
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Assume a "minimum image criterion" to build the path. If an atom moves by more than half the length of a crystal axis between one image and the next in the input (before interpolation), an appropriate periodic replica of that atom is chosen. Useful to avoid jumps in the initial reaction path. Default: .FALSE.

title: temp_req
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Temperature used for the langevin dynamics of the string. Default: 0.D0 Kelvin

title: ds
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Optimisation step length ( Hartree atomic units ). If opt_scheme=="broyden", ds is used as a guess for the diagonal part of the Jacobian matrix. Default: 1.D0

title: k_max, k_min
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Set them to use a Variable Elastic Constants scheme elastic constants are in the range [ k_min, k_max ] this is useful to rise the resolution around the saddle point. Default: 0.1D0 Hartree atomic units

title: path_thr
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: The simulation stops when the error ( the norm of the force orthogonal to the path in eV/A ) is less than path_thr. Default: 0.05D0 eV / Angstrom

title: use_masses
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: If. TRUE. the optimisation of the path is performed using mass-weighted coordinates. Useful together with quick-min optimization scheme, if some bonds are much stiffer than others. By assigning a larger (fictitious) mass to atoms with stiff bonds, one may use a longer time step "ds" Default: .FALSE.

title: use_freezing
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: If. TRUE. the images are optimised according to their error: only those images with an error larger than half of the largest are optimised. The other images are kept frozen. Default: .FALSE.

title: lfcp
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: If .TRUE. perform a constant bias potential (constant-mu) calculation with - ESM method (assume_isolated = 'esm' and esm_bc = 'bc2' or 'bc3' must be set in SYSTEM namelist) or - ESM-RISM method (assume_isolated = 'esm' and esm_bc = 'bc1' must be set set in SYSTEM namelist, and trism = .TRUE. must be set set in CONTROL namelist). fcp_mu gives the target Fermi energy. See the header of PW/src/fcp_module.f90 for documentation Default: .FALSE.

title: fcp_mu
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: If lfcp == .TRUE., gives the target Fermi energy [eV]. One can specify the total charge of the system for the first and last image by giving TOTAL_CHARGE cards so that the Fermi energy of these systems will be the target value, otherwise first_last_opt should be .TRUE. For the initial charge of intermediate images, the TOTAL_CHARGE is linearly interpolated between the initial and the final ones unless the TOTAL_CHARGE is given in the input file. Default: 0.d0

title: fcp_thr
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: The simulation stops when the error ( the maximum of the force acting on the FCP in V ) is less than fcp_thr. Default: 0.01D0 V

title: fcp_scheme
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: Specify the type of optimization scheme for FCP: 'lm' Line-Minimization method. 'newton' Newton-Raphson method with diagonal hessian matrix. Also, coupling with DIIS. 'coupled' Coupled method with ionic positions. This is available only if opt_scheme == 'broyden', or 'broyden2'. Default: 'lm' 'lm' 'newton' 'coupled'

title: index1, index2, ... indexN
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: index1, index2, ..., indexN are indices of the images to which the Climbing-Image procedure apply. If more than one image is specified they must be separated by a comma.

title: tot_charge
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: tot_charge is the total charge of the system.

title: tot_charge
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: tot_charge is the total charge of the system.

title: tot_charge
subtitle: neb.x · BEGIN
text: tot_charge is the total charge of the system.

title: pw.x with OS-CDFT
subtitle: Input reference · PWscf
text: Introduction Input data format: { } = optional, [ ] = it depends, | = or Structure of the oscdft.in file: =============================================================================== &OSCDFT ... / TARGET_OCCUPATION_NUMBERS see TARGET_OCCUPATION_NUMBERS [ GAMMA_VAL gamma_val(1) ... gamma_val(n_oscdft) ]

title: oscdft_type
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: 1 : C. Ku, P. H. L. Sit, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 15, 4781 (2019). 2 : L. Ponet, E. Di Lucente, N. Marzari, npj Comput. Mater. 10, 151 (2024). Note: For oscdft_type=2, only the keyword "occupation" and the keywords constraint_* can be used (see below). Default: 1

title: n_oscdft
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Number of entries of the TARGET_OCCUPATION_NUMBERS card.

title: get_ground_state_first
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., perform an scf calculation to convergence before applying constraint. Default: .FALSE.

title: warm_up_niter
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Runs warm_up_niter scf iterations first before applying constraint. If get_ground_state_first is .TRUE. then scf convergence is achieved first before running warm_up_niter scf iterations without applying the constraints. Default: 0

title: convergence_type
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: The variable that is checked for convergence with the convergence threshold. 'multipliers' Converges when the change in multipliers between iterations is less than the threshold. 'gradient' Converges when (occupation number - target occupation number) is less than the threshold. 'energy' Converges when the change in total energy between iterations is less than the threshold. 'always_false' Never converges (for debugging). 'always_true' Always converges (for debugging). Default: 'gradient' 'multipliers' 'gradient' 'energy' 'always_false' 'always_true'

title: iteration_type
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Order of charge density and OS-CDFT multipliers optimizations. 0 OS-CDFT multipliers optimization is a micro-iteration inside the charge density iteration. The convergence threshold of the OS-CDFT multipliers iterations can be set to start loose at max_conv_thr and gradually tighten to a minimum of min_conv_thr by multiplying the threshold with conv_thr_multiplier after every successful OS-CDFT multipliers iteration. A final convergence threshold of final_conv_thr can also be set to prevent the charge density iteration from converging when the OS-CDFT convergence test is larger than final_conv_thr. 1 Charge density optimization is a micro-iteration inside the OS-CDFT multiplier optimization. The convergence threshold of the OS-CDFT multipliers is set by max_conv_thr. min_conv_thr, conv_thr_multiplier, and final_conv_thr are ignored. 0 1

title: optimization_method
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Method to update the OS-CDFT multipliers. 'gradient descent' multipliers -= min_gamma_n * (occupation number - target occupation number) 'gradient descent2' multipliers -= gamma_val * min_gamma_n * (occupation number - target occupation number) Default: 'gradient descent' 'gradient descent' 'gradient descent2'

title: array_convergence_func
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Specify the method of multiple values to scalar for convergence test when convergence_type is either 'gradient' or 'multipliers'. 'maxval' Takes the maximum of the convergence_type before comparing with threshold. 'norm' Takes the root sum squared of the convergence_type before comparing with threshold. 'rms' Takes the root mean squared of the convergence_type before comparing with threshold. Default: 'maxval' 'maxval' 'norm' 'rms'

title: max_conv_thr
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If iteration_type is 0, this is the starting convergence threshold. If iteration_type is 1, this is the convergence threshold. See iteration_type for more explanations. Default: 1.D-1

title: min_conv_thr
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If iteration_type is 0, this is the minimum convergence threshold. If iteration_type is 1, this is ignored. See iteration_type for more explanations. Default: 1.D-3

title: final_conv_thr
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If iteration_type is 0 and final_conv_thr > 0.D0, the charge density convergence is prevented when the OS-CDFT convergence test is larger than final_conv_thr. Otherwise, this is ignored. Default: -1.D0

title: conv_thr_multiplier
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If iteration_type is 0, see iteration_type for explanations. Otherwise, this is ignored. Default: 0.5D0

title: print_occupation_matrix
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., prints the occupation matrices. Default: .FALSE.

title: print_occupation_eigenvectors
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., prints the occupation eigenvectors. Default: .FALSE.

title: min_gamma_n
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Learning rate of optimizations. See optimization_method. Default: 1.D0

title: has_min_multiplier
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., sets the minimum value of the OS-CDFT multipliers to min_multiplier. Default: .FALSE.

title: min_multiplier
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Minimum value of the OS-CDFT multipliers. Enabled using has_min_multiplier

title: has_max_multiplier
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., sets the maximum value of the OS-CDFT multipliers to max_multiplier. Default: .FALSE.

title: max_multiplier
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Maximum value of the OS-CDFT multipliers. Enabled using has_max_multiplier

title: miniter
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Minimum OS-CDFT iterations. Default: 0

title: maxiter
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: Maximum OS-CDFT iterations. Default: 0

title: swapping_technique
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: See https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00281 'none' No swapping technique. Always chooses the occupation number in ascending order. 'permute' Chooses the occupation number associated with the occupation eigenvector that is most similar compared to previous iteration (using dot product) Default: 'none' 'none' 'permute'

title: debug_print
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., prints additional debug informations. Default: .FALSE.

title: orthogonalize_swfc
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
text: If .TRUE., uses Lowdin orthogonalized atomic orbitals. Default: .FALSE.

title: normalize_swfc
subtitle: pw.x with OS-CDFT · &OSCDFT
